review_notes: I read the whole file and the one downstream user, SobolevPoincareBall.lean around lines 630–700. I also checked the `classicalGradient_apply` simp lemma in Cutoff/Basic.lean. I found no simp lemma, simp attribute or `@[simp]` declaration for `seeleyAffineMap`. Its unfolding is done by hand in several places in the file and in the downstream proof. I did not find a rewrite cycle or competing rules. I did not run Lean, so I can't say whether the proposed lemma would shorten any particular proof.

findings.excerpt: def seeleyAffineMap (x₀ : Vec 3) (r : ℝ) (x : Vec 3) : Vec 3 :=
findings.problem: `seeleyAffineMap` is a plain `def` with no simp lemma that gives its pointwise value `x₀ + r • x`. Every proof therefore unfolds it ad hoc. In this file, `seeleyAffineMap_preimage` uses `dsimp [seeleyAffineMap]` twice, and `seeleyAffine_fderiv` ends with `simp [seeleyAffineMap]`. `seeleyAffineMap_volume` proves a `hcomp` equation by `funext y; rfl`. `seeleyAffineMap_measurableEmbedding` uses `change MeasurableEmbedding (fun x : Vec 3 => x₀ + r • x)`. `seeleyAffine_fderiv` has a similar `hcomp` by `rfl`. The downstream proof in SobolevPoincareBall.lean does the same with `change ContDiff ℝ 1 (fun x : Vec 3 => x₀ + r • x)` and `simpa [F]`. The simp interface lacks the canonical unfolding lemma, so users depend on definitional unfolding.
findings.proposed_change: Right after the definition, add `@[simp] theorem seeleyAffineMap_apply (x₀ : Vec 3) (r : ℝ) (x : Vec 3) : seeleyAffineMap x₀ r x = x₀ + r • x := rfl`. It could also be stated for `0` and `1`, but the pointwise lemma is the minimum. This is safe for simp because the right-hand side contains no `seeleyAffineMap`, so it can't loop, and `+` and `•` are the intended normal form. Then replace the `dsimp [seeleyAffineMap]` and `simp [seeleyAffineMap]` calls with `simp`, or with `rw [seeleyAffineMap_apply]`. Replace the `change ... (fun x => x₀ + r • x)` steps and the `funext y; rfl` equations with `simp` or `simp [Function.comp_def]`. Callers can then stop unfolding a `let F := seeleyAffineMap x₀ r`.
findings.benefit: The value of the affine map has one canonical, named rewrite rule. Proofs about the scaling map no longer need `change`, `rfl` or definition-unfolding simp sets. Downstream files can use plain `simp` and don't have to know the definition's internal form.
